title: PowerToys breaks win32 system menu showing on app with custom titlebar
summary: A custom Win32 title bar reports an invalid system-menu handle when Always On Top is enabled.

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied the menu-handling sequence, diagnostic ZIP and an Always On Top on/off comparison; the mechanism remains unconfirmed.
evidence: On 0.99.1, the reported custom-title-bar application gets ERROR_INVALID_MENU_HANDLE from TrackPopupMenu on one machine; disabling Always On Top restores behavior.
The report includes code excerpts and a bug report ZIP; a complete standalone sample is not supplied.
Current AlwaysOnTop.cpp obtains a system menu and adds or updates an Always On Top entry; this is a relevant boundary, not proof it invalidates a handle.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce using the reported menu-handling sequence and isolate the interaction before proposing a narrowly scoped correction.

fix_assessment.rationale: A targeted menu-lifecycle correction is applicable if the interaction is reproduced; no specific causal call is confirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate Always On Top custom system-menu interaction
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a system-menu update or lifecycle interaction interferes with a custom title bar; no particular invalidating call is established.
plan: Reproduce with a minimal custom-title-bar window based on the provided snippets and compare module-enabled and disabled behavior.
Trace GetSystemMenu, menu update events, TrackPopupMenu results and handle lifecycle without assuming a race.
Correct only the demonstrated interference while retaining the Always On Top menu command and normal window handling.
Add coverage for custom and standard title bars, menu open/close, toggling the setting, and repeated interactions.
verification: The custom title bar opens its menu repeatedly without ERROR_INVALID_MENU_HANDLE with Always On Top enabled.
The Always On Top command still toggles correctly on supported standard windows and disabling the feature removes its entry.

confidence.rationale: The on/off comparison is useful, but the report is machine-specific and the triggering operation has not been reproduced.

information_gaps.information: Which menu operation or event precedes the invalid handle on a current build.

reproduce.title: Compare custom system menus with Always On Top enabled
reproduce.version_requirement: Use the current PowerToys release; compare 0.99.1 if needed.
prerequisites: Use a Windows test machine and a minimal Win32 window implementing the title-bar and WM_NCRBUTTONUP menu sequence in the issue.
setup: Enable Always On Top and its system-menu integration; preserve the ability to disable the module as a control.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Create a minimal Win32 test app using the issue’s DwmExtendFrameIntoClientArea, WM_NCCALCSIZE and HTCAPTION handling, then GetSystemMenu and TrackPopupMenu in WM_NCRBUTTONUP; report return values and GetLastError.
steps: 1. Launch the test window and repeatedly right-click its title bar with Always On Top enabled.
2. Record GetSystemMenu and TrackPopupMenu results, error code and menu-event sequence.
3. Disable Always On Top and repeat; compare a standard title-bar window and an independently restarted Explorer session if required.
reproduce.expected_result: The custom window opens a valid system menu each time and its commands remain usable with or without Always On Top.
